title: It was the music of something beginning… #Ragtime #NewYorkCityCenter ...
transcript: Ragtime is, in my opinion, one of the greatest American musicals ever written. And I also don't know that there's ever been a better time for a production of ragtime because so many of its themes feel so relevant to the America of today. Which is why I was so excited when New York City Center announced that they would be doing ragtime as their annual gala performance. And even more excited when they announced the cast because we got Josh Henry, Casey Levi, Brendan Uranowitz, Ben Levi Ross, like some of my all time favorite performers. And I am happy to report that this production did not disappoint. And getting to hear these voices sing this score, which is absolutely gorgeous with a full orchestra, is just a true gift. Josh Henry in particular as Coalhouse Walker is just unbelievably good, as he often is. And yes, it is incredibly minimal in its design, even by city center standards. So definitely don't go in expect acting a lavish ragtime revival, but what you will get is a production of ragtime that sounds stunning. Maybe the best it has ever sounded since the original cast. And add on top of that how topical a lot of its themes feel. And do you have a truly special production? One that I would definitely recommend you get tickets to, except for the fact that I'm pretty sure is almost completely sold out. Certainly the cheap seats in the balcony are, but if you Do get to see this production. Know that you are in for something truly special. And I'm just crossing my fingers for at least a cast recording, because this needs to be preserved in some way.
classificationReason: Creator attended and reviewed a Ragtime production at New York City Center, sharing detailed opinions about the cast, performances, and production quality with clear first-hand experience
